messages:
ian-customer: Hey team — found what looks like one of our API keys in a public GitHub gist that a contractor uploaded. Can someone help with immediate rotation and scope/impact checks? :rotating_light:
sara-support: sorry to hear that — hmm. Can you paste the repo/gist link (no secrets) and the org id? We can start a rotation and check audit logs. :lock:
ian-customer: https://gist.github.com/xxx (I removed the key itself). Org: org_92x. The key was created 2025-11-03. Not sure if it was used.
sara-support: copying the standard playbook steps: 1) rotate/revoke the leaked key, 2) create a replacement key with least privilege, 3) inspect audit logs for any requests, 4) rotate any other secrets that may be co-located. I'm starting step 1 now.
sara-support: @mike-security can you join to help with logs and any compliance notification?
mike-security: on it. First pass: I will check audit logs and billing spikes. If you can tell me the last 24h timestamp range to prioritize, that helps.
nada-ops: (deploy-bot) scheduled job: creating investigation ticket INF-2026-342 and attaching gist link.
ian-customer: last active commit on the gist was ~6 hours ago. No obvious calls from our infra that I can see but I'm not the primary on logs.
sara-support: rotating now — creating replacement key with reduced scopes. Command we used in console UI: Console > Team > API keys > New key (Name: rotated-from-gist). Recommend updating envs immediately.
sara-support: quick CLI snippet for rotation (internal):
```bash
# create new key
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/admin/keys 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"name":"rotated-from-gist","scopes":["inference:invoke"],"expires_at":null}'
# revoke old key
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/admin/keys/revoke 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
  -d '{"key_id":"<old-key-id>"}'
```
mike-security: I pulled audit logs for org_92x. No successful requests using the leaked key in the last 48h. There are 3 failed auth attempts from two IPs (likely scanning). I've attached the IPs to the ticket. If those IPs keep showing, we can block at edge.
nada-ops: For customers on Private deployments using our KMS/HSM integration: rotating the Redwood API key is still necessary, but please also check customer-managed KMS for any leaked plaintext secrets. If they used our Secrets API to store the key, we should verify access logs on the KMS/HSM.
sara-support: noted. @ian-customer please confirm if the leaked content included any .env files or IAM creds for cloud providers — those would be higher priority.
ian-customer: just the single API key line that I saw, no provider creds. It was in a README snippet.
mike-security: next steps from sec: 1) keep old key revoked (done), 2) monitor audit logs for 72h, 3) generate a short incident summary for compliance. If customer data was accessed we escalate to legal — at the moment no evidence of data exfiltration.
sara-support: I've pushed rotated key to your team owner via secure channel. Please rotate any copies in deployment manifests, CI/CD, and local dev machines. Also enable key restrictions (IP, referrer) and set quota limits.
ian-customer: thanks — one question: is there an API to rotate keys programmatically so we can automate this in our CI?
sara-support: yes, the Admin Keys API supports create/revoke. We'll share internal docs in the ticket. For automation we recommend a short TTL + orchestration in your secrets manager.
mike-security: for compliance — mark INF-2026-342 as "security: leaked key" and attach audit logs; I'll draft the incident summary.
sara-support: closing loop: old key revoked at 1764209950, new key issued at 1764209972. Please confirm after you update runtimes. :white_check_mark:
ian-customer: confirmed updated in CI and staging. No errors so far. Thanks for the quick help.
mike-security: will keep monitoring; if anything shows up we'll ping the channel. Great coordination. :thumbsup:
